source.text: וַיְהִ֗י אַחַר֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה וְהָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים נִסָּ֖ה אֶת־אַבְרָהָ֑ם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו אַבְרָהָ֖ם וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הִנֵּֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was after these things, and God tested Abraham, and said to him, Abraham. And he said, here I [am].

en.L: And after these things God tested Abraham and said to him, "Abraham!" And he said, "Here I am."
en.B: Some time after this, God put Abraham to the test. "Abraham!" {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called, and Abraham answered, "Here I am."
en.R: Later on, God put Abraham to a test. God called to him, "Abraham!" Abraham answered, "Yes, I am here."

es.L: Y sucedió después de estas cosas que Dios probó a Abraham y le dijo: «¡Abraham!». Y él dijo: «Aquí estoy».
es.B: Pasado algún tiempo, Dios sometió a prueba a Abraham. «¡Abraham!», lo llamó, y Abraham respondió: «Aquí estoy».
es.R: Tiempo después, Dios puso a prueba a Abraham. Dios lo llamó: «¡Abraham!». Abraham contestó: «Sí, aquí estoy».

fr.L: Et après ces choses, Dieu mit Abraham à l’épreuve et lui dit : « Abraham ! » Et il dit : « Me voici. »
fr.B: Quelque temps après, Dieu mit Abraham à l’épreuve. « Abraham ! » appela-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}, et Abraham répondit : « Me voici. »
fr.R: Plus tard, Dieu a mis Abraham à l’épreuve. Dieu l’a appelé : « Abraham ! » Abraham a répondu : « Oui, je suis là. »

sw.L: Ikawa baada ya mambo haya, Mungu akamjaribu Abrahamu, akamwambia, "Abrahamu!" Naye akasema, "Mimi hapa."
sw.B: Muda fulani baadaye, Mungu alimjaribu Abrahamu. Akamwita, "Abrahamu!" Naye Abrahamu akaitika, "Mimi hapa."
sw.R: Baadaye Mungu alimpa Abrahamu mtihani. Mungu akamwita, "Abrahamu!" Abrahamu akajibu, "Naam, niko hapa."

decisions.choice: tested (nissah): put to the proof
decisions.reason: To test is to prove what is in someone, whether they will trust and obey (Exodus 20:20; Deuteronomy 8:2). The narrator tells the reader at once that this is a test; Abraham does not know it. God does not tempt anyone to do evil (James 1:13).

decisions.choice: Here I am (hinneni): ready to hear and obey
decisions.reason: The answer means 'I am listening, at your service'. Abraham says it three times in this chapter: to God (verse 1), to Isaac (verse 7), and to the angel (verse 11).

decisions.choice: after these things: a new episode
decisions.reason: The phrase links this story loosely to what has gone before (15:1). Isaac is now old enough to carry the wood (verse 6).

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("mit à l'épreuve", "répondit"), passé composé at Readable ("a mis à l'épreuve", "a répondu")
decisions.reason: As the French style guide sets out: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and read in school today. Speech keeps the tenses of speech at every level.

source.text: וַיֹּ֡אמֶר קַח־נָ֠א אֶת־בִּנְךָ֨אֶת־יְחִֽידְךָ֤ אֲשֶׁר־אָהַ֨בְתָּ֙ אֶת־יִצְחָ֔ק וְלֶךְ־לְךָ֔ אֶל־אֶ֖רֶץ הַמֹּרִיָּ֑ה וְהַעֲלֵ֤הוּ שָׁם֙ לְעֹלָ֔ה עַ֚ל אַחַ֣ד הֶֽהָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֹמַ֥ר אֵלֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, take, please, your son, your only one, whom you love, Isaac, and go for yourself to [the] land of Moriah, and offer him up there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains which I will tell you.

en.L: And he said, "Please take your son, your only [son], whom you love, Isaac, and go to the land of Moriah, and offer him up there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains of which I will tell you."
en.B: God said, "Please take your son, your only son, the one you love, Isaac. Go to the land of Moriah, and there, on one of the mountains that I will point out to you, offer him up as a burnt offering."
en.R: God said, "Take your son Isaac, your only son, the son you love. Go to the land of Moriah. There, on a mountain I will show you, give him to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as a burnt offering, a sacrifice burned on the altar."

es.L: Y dijo: «Toma, te ruego, a tu hijo, a tu único, a quien amas, a Isaac, y ve a la tierra de Moria, y ofrécelo allí en holocausto sobre uno de los montes que yo te diré».
es.B: Dios le dijo: «Toma a tu hijo, a tu único hijo, al que amas, a Isaac. Ve a la tierra de Moria, y allí, sobre uno de los montes que yo te indicaré, ofrécelo en holocausto».
es.R: Dios le dijo: «Toma a tu hijo Isaac, tu único hijo, el hijo que amas. Ve a la tierra de Moria. Allí, en un monte que yo te mostraré, ofrécemelo en holocausto, es decir, en un sacrificio quemado sobre el altar».

fr.L: Et il dit : « Prends donc ton fils, ton unique, que tu aimes, Isaac, et va-t’en au pays de Moria, et là offre-le en holocauste sur l’une des montagnes que je te dirai. »
fr.B: Dieu dit : « Prends, je t’en prie, ton fils, ton fils unique, celui que tu aimes, Isaac. Va au pays de Moria, et là, sur l’une des montagnes que je t’indiquerai, offre-le en holocauste. »
fr.R: Dieu a dit : « Prends ton fils Isaac, ton fils unique, le fils que tu aimes. Va au pays de Moria. Là, sur une montagne que je te montrerai, donne-le-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} en holocauste, c’est-à-dire en sacrifice brûlé sur l’autel. »

sw.L: Akasema, "Twaa sasa mwanao, mwana wako wa pekee, umpendaye, Isaka, uende zako hadi nchi ya Moria, ukamtoe huko kuwa sadaka ya kuteketezwa juu ya mmojawapo wa milima nitakayokuambia."
sw.B: Mungu akasema, "Tafadhali mchukue mwanao, mwana wako wa pekee, yule unayempenda, Isaka. Nenda katika nchi ya Moria, na huko, juu ya mmojawapo wa milima nitakayokuonyesha, umtoe kuwa sadaka ya kuteketezwa."
sw.R: Mungu akasema, "Mchukue mwanao Isaka, mwana wako wa pekee, mwana unayempenda. Nenda katika nchi ya Moria. Huko, juu ya mlima nitakaokuonyesha, unitolee yeye kuwa sadaka ya kuteketezwa, yaani sadaka inayochomwa juu ya madhabahu."

decisions.choice: your son, your only son, whom you love, Isaac: each word closer
decisions.reason: The command names the son step by step, each phrase tightening the hold: your son, your only one, the one you love, Isaac. The word 'love' appears here for the first time in the Bible.

decisions.choice: your only son (yachid): the one son left, the son of the promise
decisions.reason: Ishmael has been sent away (21:14), and Isaac is the only son through whom the promise will come (21:12). The word is used of an only child (Judges 11:34; Zechariah 12:10).

decisions.choice: go (lekh lekha): the words of Abraham's first call
decisions.reason: The unusual phrase 'go for yourself' is found only here and in 12:1, where God told Abraham to leave his country. Both calls ask him to give up what is dearest, and both send him to a place God will show him.

decisions.choice: Moriah ... a burnt offering
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 3:1 places Solomon's temple on 'Mount Moriah' in Jerusalem. A burnt offering (olah) was wholly burned on the altar, nothing kept back. Child sacrifice was practiced among Israel's neighbors, and the Law later condemns it as an abomination (Leviticus 18:21; Deuteronomy 12:31; Jeremiah 7:31).

decisions.choice: a sacrifice burned on the altar
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a burnt offering was.

decisions.choice: "ofrécemelo" with no deity pronoun span
decisions.reason: The English Readable marks "me" for the deity pronoun setting. In Spanish the pronoun is joined to the verb ("ofrécemelo"), and a clitic joined to the verb takes no span, so Spanish has none here.

source.text: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֨ם אַבְרָהָ֜ם בַּבֹּ֗קֶר וַֽיַּחֲבֹשׁ֙ אֶת־חֲמֹר֔וֹ וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶת־שְׁנֵ֤י נְעָרָיו֙ אִתּ֔וֹ וְאֵ֖ת יִצְחָ֣ק בְּנ֑וֹ וַיְבַקַּע֙ עֲצֵ֣י עֹלָ֔ה וַיָּ֣קָם וַיֵּ֔לֶךְ אֶל־הַמָּק֖וֹם אֲשֶׁר־אָֽמַר־ל֥וֹ הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And rose early Abraham in the morning and saddled his donkey, and took two of his young men with him and Isaac his son; and split [the] wood of [the] burnt offering and arose and went to the place which had said to him God.

en.L: So Abraham rose early in the morning and saddled his donkey, and took two of his young men with him, and Isaac his son. And he split the wood for the burnt offering, and rose and went to the place of which God had told him.
en.B: Abraham was up at dawn. He saddled his donkey and took along two of his young men, and his son Isaac. After splitting wood for the burnt offering, he started out for the place God had named to him.
en.R: The next morning Abraham got up early. He put a saddle on his donkey. He took his son Isaac and two of his young servants with him. He chopped wood for the burnt offering. Then they set off toward the place God had spoken of.

es.L: Y madrugó Abraham por la mañana y ensilló su asno, y tomó consigo a dos de sus jóvenes y a Isaac su hijo. Y partió la leña para el holocausto, y se levantó y fue al lugar que Dios le había dicho.
es.B: Abraham se levantó al amanecer. Ensilló su asno y llevó consigo a dos de sus jóvenes y a su hijo Isaac. Después de partir leña para el holocausto, se puso en camino hacia el lugar que Dios le había indicado.
es.R: A la mañana siguiente, Abraham se levantó temprano. Le puso la montura a su burro. Llevó consigo a su hijo Isaac y a dos de sus jóvenes sirvientes. Cortó leña para el holocausto. Luego se pusieron en camino hacia el lugar del que Dios le había hablado.

fr.L: Et Abraham se leva tôt le matin et sella son âne, et il prit avec lui deux de ses jeunes gens, et Isaac son fils. Et il fendit le bois de l’holocauste, et il se leva et alla vers le lieu dont Dieu lui avait parlé.
fr.B: Abraham se leva à l’aube. Il sella son âne et emmena deux de ses jeunes gens, ainsi que son fils Isaac. Après avoir fendu du bois pour l’holocauste, il partit pour le lieu que Dieu lui avait indiqué.
fr.R: Le lendemain, Abraham s’est levé tôt. Il a mis une selle sur son âne. Il a pris avec lui son fils Isaac et deux de ses jeunes serviteurs. Il a coupé du bois pour l’holocauste. Puis ils sont partis vers l’endroit dont Dieu avait parlé.

sw.L: Basi Abrahamu akaamka mapema asubuhi, akatandika punda wake, akawachukua vijana wake wawili pamoja naye, na Isaka mwanawe. Akapasua kuni za sadaka ya kuteketezwa, akainuka, akaenda mahali ambapo Mungu alimwambia.
sw.B: Abrahamu aliamka alfajiri. Akatandika punda wake, akawachukua vijana wake wawili, pamoja na mwanawe Isaka. Baada ya kupasua kuni za sadaka ya kuteketezwa, akaondoka kwenda mahali ambapo Mungu alikuwa amemtajia.
sw.R: Kesho yake Abrahamu aliamka asubuhi na mapema. Akaweka tandiko juu ya punda wake. Akamchukua mwanawe Isaka na watumishi wake wawili vijana. Akakata kuni za sadaka ya kuteketezwa. Kisha wakaondoka kwenda mahali ambapo Mungu alikuwa amesema.

decisions.choice: Abraham rose early in the morning: the words of 21:14
decisions.reason: The same words began the morning when Abraham sent Ishmael away. Abraham says nothing and does not delay; the narrator gives only his actions.

decisions.choice: young men (na'ar): servants
decisions.reason: The word means a boy or young man, and often a young servant. It is the same word used of Isaac in verse 5.

decisions.choice: young men (L, B), young servants (R)
decisions.reason: Na'ar is not the word for a slave (eved); Literal and Balanced keep 'young men' and Readable 'young servants'.

source.text: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֗י וַיִּשָּׂ֨א אַבְרָהָ֧ם אֶת־עֵינָ֛יו וַיַּ֥רְא אֶת־הַמָּק֖וֹם מֵרָחֹֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: On the third day, and lifted Abraham his eyes and saw the place from afar.

en.L: On the third day Abraham lifted up his eyes and saw the place from afar.
en.B: On the third day Abraham raised his eyes and caught sight of the place far away.
en.R: After traveling for three days, Abraham looked up and saw the place, still far away.

es.L: Al tercer día alzó Abraham sus ojos y vio el lugar de lejos.
es.B: Al tercer día, Abraham levantó la vista y divisó el lugar a lo lejos.
es.R: Después de tres días de viaje, Abraham miró hacia adelante y vio el lugar, que todavía estaba lejos.

fr.L: Le troisième jour, Abraham leva les yeux et vit le lieu de loin.
fr.B: Le troisième jour, Abraham leva les yeux et aperçut le lieu au loin.
fr.R: Après trois jours de voyage, Abraham a levé les yeux et il a vu l’endroit, encore loin.

sw.L: Siku ya tatu Abrahamu akainua macho yake, akapaona mahali pale kwa mbali.
sw.B: Siku ya tatu Abrahamu aliinua macho, akapaona mahali pale kwa mbali.
sw.R: Baada ya kusafiri siku tatu, Abrahamu alitazama juu, akapaona mahali pale, bado mbali.

decisions.choice: on the third day: a long journey
decisions.reason: Beersheba (21:33) lies about fifty miles (eighty kilometers) from Jerusalem, a journey of some three days on foot. Abraham has had three days to think.

decisions.choice: lifted up his eyes: looked up
decisions.reason: The phrase means to look up or to look into the distance (13:10; 18:2).

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֶל־נְעָרָ֗יו שְׁבוּ־לָכֶ֥ם פֹּה֙ עִֽם־הַחֲמ֔וֹר וַאֲנִ֣י וְהַנַּ֔עַר נֵלְכָ֖ה עַד־כֹּ֑ה וְנִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֖ה וְנָשׁ֥וּבָה אֲלֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Abraham to his young men, stay here with the donkey, and I and the lad will go up to there, and we will worship and we will return to you.

en.L: And Abraham said to his young men, "Stay here with the donkey; I and the boy will go over there, and we will worship and come back to you."
en.B: Then Abraham told his young men, "You wait here with the donkey. The boy and I are going on up there to worship, and afterward we will return to you."
en.R: Abraham told his servants, "Stay here with the donkey. My son and I will go up there and worship God. Then we will both come back to you."

es.L: Y dijo Abraham a sus jóvenes: «{{plural_you:Quédense|Quedaos}} aquí con el asno; yo y el muchacho iremos hasta allá, y adoraremos y volveremos {{plural_you:a ustedes|a vosotros}}».
es.B: Entonces Abraham les dijo a sus jóvenes: «{{plural_you:Esperen|Esperad}} aquí con el asno. El muchacho y yo vamos a subir hasta allá para adorar, y después volveremos {{plural_you:con ustedes|con vosotros}}».
es.R: Abraham les dijo a sus sirvientes: «{{plural_you:Quédense|Quedaos}} aquí con el burro. Mi hijo y yo vamos a subir allá para adorar a Dios. Después los dos volveremos {{plural_you:con ustedes|con vosotros}}».

fr.L: Et Abraham dit à ses jeunes gens : « Restez ici avec l’âne ; moi et le garçon, nous irons jusque là-bas, et nous adorerons et nous reviendrons vers vous. »
fr.B: Puis Abraham dit à ses jeunes gens : « Attendez ici avec l’âne. Le garçon et moi, nous allons monter là-haut pour adorer, et ensuite nous reviendrons vers vous. »
fr.R: Abraham a dit à ses serviteurs : « Restez ici avec l’âne. Mon fils et moi, nous allons monter là-haut pour adorer Dieu. Puis nous reviendrons tous les deux vers vous. »

sw.L: Naye Abrahamu akawaambia vijana wake, "Kaeni hapa pamoja na punda; mimi na kijana tutakwenda kule, nasi tutaabudu, kisha tutarudi kwenu."
sw.B: Kisha Abrahamu akawaambia vijana wake, "Ninyi ngojeni hapa pamoja na punda. Mimi na kijana tunakwenda kule juu kuabudu, na baadaye tutarudi kwenu."
sw.R: Abrahamu akawaambia watumishi wake, "Kaeni hapa na punda. Mimi na mwanangu tutakwenda kule juu kumwabudu Mungu. Kisha sote wawili tutarudi kwenu."

decisions.choice: worship (hishtachaveh): bow down
decisions.reason: The verb means to bow low before someone, and so to worship.

decisions.choice: we will come back to you: both of them
decisions.reason: Abraham says 'we will return'. Whether he says it to keep the servants from suspecting, or in trust that God would give Isaac back, the text does not say. Hebrews 11:19 reads it as faith that God could raise the dead.

decisions.choice: My son ... both
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear who 'the boy' is and that 'we' means both of them.

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֶת־עֲצֵ֣י הָעֹלָ֗ה וַיָּ֨שֶׂם֙ עַל־יִצְחָ֣ק בְּנ֔וֹ וַיִּקַּ֣ח בְּיָד֔וֹ אֶת־הָאֵ֖שׁ וְאֶת־הַֽמַּאֲכֶ֑לֶת וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם יַחְדָּֽו׃

records.literal_gloss: And took Abraham [the] wood of the burnt offering and laid [it] on Isaac his son, and took in his hand the fire and the knife; and went the two of them together.

en.L: And Abraham took the wood of the burnt offering and laid [it] on Isaac his son, and he took in his hand the fire and the knife. And the two of them went on together.
en.B: Abraham loaded the wood for the burnt offering onto his son Isaac and carried the fire and the knife in his own hand, and the two of them walked on side by side.
en.R: Abraham gave Isaac the wood to carry. Abraham carried the fire and the knife. The two of them walked on together.

es.L: Y tomó Abraham la leña del holocausto y [la] puso sobre Isaac su hijo, y tomó en su mano el fuego y el cuchillo; y fueron los dos juntos.
es.B: Abraham cargó la leña del holocausto sobre su hijo Isaac y llevó en su propia mano el fuego y el cuchillo, y los dos siguieron caminando juntos.
es.R: Abraham le dio a Isaac la leña para que la llevara. Abraham llevaba el fuego y el cuchillo. Los dos siguieron caminando juntos.

fr.L: Et Abraham prit le bois de l’holocauste et [le] mit sur Isaac son fils, et il prit dans sa main le feu et le couteau. Et ils allèrent tous les deux ensemble.
fr.B: Abraham chargea le bois de l’holocauste sur son fils Isaac et porta lui-même à la main le feu et le couteau, et tous deux poursuivirent leur chemin côte à côte.
fr.R: Abraham a donné le bois à porter à Isaac. Abraham, lui, portait le feu et le couteau. Ils ont continué leur chemin tous les deux ensemble.

sw.L: Naye Abrahamu akatwaa kuni za sadaka ya kuteketezwa, akamtwika Isaka mwanawe, akashika mkononi mwake moto na kisu; nao wakaenda wote wawili pamoja.
sw.B: Abrahamu alimtwika mwanawe Isaka kuni za sadaka ya kuteketezwa, naye mwenyewe akabeba mkononi moto na kisu, nao wawili wakaendelea kutembea bega kwa bega.
sw.R: Abrahamu akampa Isaka kuni azibebe. Abrahamu mwenyewe akabeba moto na kisu. Wawili hao wakaendelea kutembea pamoja.

decisions.choice: the fire: coals carried in a pot
decisions.reason: Fire was carried as burning coals in a clay pot or on a dish, to light the offering.

decisions.choice: the knife (ma'akhelet): a butcher's knife
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb 'eat' and means a large knife for cutting meat (Judges 19:29).

decisions.choice: the two of them went on together
decisions.reason: The phrase is repeated in verse 8, framing the only words between father and son. Christian readers have long compared Isaac carrying the wood to Jesus carrying his cross (John 19:17).

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יִצְחָ֜ק אֶל־אַבְרָהָ֤ם אָבִיו֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אָבִ֔י וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הִנֶּ֣נִּֽי בְנִ֑י וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּ֤ה הָאֵשׁ֙ וְהָ֣עֵצִ֔ים וְאַיֵּ֥ה הַשֶּׂ֖ה לְעֹלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Isaac to Abraham his father, and said, my father. And he said, here I [am], my son. And he said, here [are] the fire and the wood, and where [is] the lamb for a burnt offering?

en.L: And Isaac said to Abraham his father, "My father!" And he said, "Here I am, my son." And he said, "Look, the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb for a burnt offering?"
en.B: Isaac said to his father Abraham, "My father." "I am here, my son," he answered. "I see the fire and the wood," said Isaac, "but where is the lamb to be offered?"
en.R: Isaac said to Abraham, "Father?" Abraham answered, "Yes, my son, what is it?" Isaac said, "Here is the fire, and here is the wood. But where is the lamb we will offer to God?"

es.L: Y dijo Isaac a Abraham su padre: «¡Padre mío!». Y él dijo: «Aquí estoy, hijo mío». Y dijo: «He aquí el fuego y la leña, pero ¿dónde está el cordero para el holocausto?».
es.B: Isaac le dijo a su padre Abraham: «Padre». «Aquí estoy, hijo mío», le respondió. «Veo el fuego y la leña», dijo Isaac, «pero ¿dónde está el cordero que vamos a ofrecer?».
es.R: Isaac le dijo a Abraham: «¿Papá?». Abraham le contestó: «Sí, hijo, ¿qué pasa?». Isaac dijo: «Aquí está el fuego, y aquí está la leña. Pero ¿dónde está el cordero que vamos a ofrecer a Dios?».

fr.L: Et Isaac dit à Abraham son père : « Mon père ! » Et il dit : « Me voici, mon fils. » Et il dit : « Voici le feu et le bois, mais où est l’agneau pour l’holocauste ? »
fr.B: Isaac dit à son père Abraham : « Mon père. » « Je suis là, mon fils », répondit-il. « Je vois le feu et le bois, dit Isaac, mais où est l’agneau à offrir ? »
fr.R: Isaac a dit à Abraham : « Papa ? » Abraham a répondu : « Oui, mon fils, qu’y a-t-il ? » Isaac a dit : « Voici le feu, et voici le bois. Mais où est l’agneau que nous allons offrir à Dieu ? »

sw.L: Naye Isaka akamwambia Abrahamu baba yake, "Baba yangu!" Naye akasema, "Mimi hapa, mwanangu." Akasema, "Tazama, moto na kuni, lakini yuko wapi mwanakondoo wa sadaka ya kuteketezwa?"
sw.B: Isaka akamwambia baba yake Abrahamu, "Baba yangu." Akajibu, "Niko hapa, mwanangu." Isaka akasema, "Moto na kuni ninaviona, lakini mwanakondoo wa kutoa sadaka yuko wapi?"
sw.R: Isaka akamwambia Abrahamu, "Baba?" Abrahamu akajibu, "Naam, mwanangu, kuna nini?" Isaka akasema, "Moto uko hapa, na kuni ziko hapa. Lakini yuko wapi mwanakondoo tutakayemtoa sadaka kwa Mungu?"

decisions.choice: the lamb (seh): a young sheep or goat
decisions.reason: The word means one animal from the flock, a sheep or a goat. A young animal was the usual burnt offering (Exodus 12:5; 29:38).

decisions.choice: Here I am, my son: the same answer as to God
decisions.reason: Abraham gives Isaac the same ready answer he gave God (verse 1). He is caught between the God who calls him and the son who calls him.

decisions.choice: we will offer to God
decisions.reason: Readable says what the lamb was for.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אַבְרָהָ֔ם אֱלֹהִ֞ים יִרְאֶה־לּ֥וֹ הַשֶּׂ֛ה לְעֹלָ֖ה בְּנִ֑י וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם יַחְדָּֽו׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Abraham, God will see for himself the lamb for a burnt offering, my son. And went the two of them together.

en.L: And Abraham said, "God will provide for {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} the lamb for a burnt offering, my son." And the two of them went on together.
en.B: Abraham answered, "God will see to the lamb for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} burnt offering, my son." And the two of them walked on together.
en.R: Abraham answered, "My son, God will provide the lamb for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} burnt offering." And the two of them kept walking together.

es.L: Y dijo Abraham: «Dios proveerá para {{deity_pronoun:sí mismo|Sí mismo}} el cordero para el holocausto, hijo mío». Y fueron los dos juntos.
es.B: Abraham respondió: «Dios se encargará del cordero para {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} holocausto, hijo mío». Y los dos siguieron caminando juntos.
es.R: Abraham le contestó: «Hijo mío, Dios dará el cordero para {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} holocausto». Y los dos siguieron caminando juntos.

fr.L: Et Abraham dit : « Dieu pourvoira {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} à l’agneau pour l’holocauste, mon fils. » Et ils allèrent tous les deux ensemble.
fr.B: Abraham répondit : « C’est Dieu qui veillera à l’agneau de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} holocauste, mon fils. » Et tous deux poursuivirent leur chemin ensemble.
fr.R: Abraham a répondu : « Mon fils, Dieu va donner l’agneau pour {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} holocauste. » Et ils ont continué à marcher tous les deux ensemble.

sw.L: Naye Abrahamu akasema, "Mungu atajipatia mwanakondoo wa sadaka ya kuteketezwa, mwanangu." Nao wakaenda wote wawili pamoja.
sw.B: Abrahamu akajibu, "Mungu atashughulikia mwanakondoo wa sadaka {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ya kuteketezwa, mwanangu." Nao wawili wakaendelea kutembea pamoja.
sw.R: Abrahamu akajibu, "Mwanangu, Mungu atatoa mwanakondoo wa sadaka {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ya kuteketezwa." Nao wawili wakaendelea kutembea pamoja.

decisions.choice: God will provide for himself: literally 'God will see for himself'
decisions.reason: The verb is 'see' (ra'ah). To 'see' something for someone means to look it out, to see to it, and so to provide it (1 Samuel 16:1, 'I have seen for myself a king'). The same verb gives the place its name (verse 14).

decisions.choice: Abraham's answer says more than he knows
decisions.reason: Abraham answers without telling Isaac what God has commanded. His words prove truer than he can see: God does provide the animal (verse 13).

decisions.choice: provide (L, R), see to (B)
decisions.reason: 'God will see' would be misread as 'God will watch'; the levels give the sense, and Balanced keeps the verb 'see' in 'see to' (m1).

decisions.choice: "proveerá para sí mismo" (L), "se encargará de" (B), "dará" (R)
decisions.reason: Spanish "ver" would read as 'watch'; Literal says "proveerá" and keeps 'for himself' as "para sí mismo", Balanced says "se encargará de" ('will see to'). The same verbs return in the name of the place (verse 14).

decisions.choice: "pourvoira lui-même à" (L), "veillera à" (B), "va donner" (R)
decisions.reason: French "voir" cannot carry the sense 'see to, provide', so Literal says "pourvoira" and Balanced "veillera à" ('watch over, see to'), which keeps the idea of looking out for something; the same verbs return in the name of the place (verse 14). "Lui-même" carries the Hebrew 'for himself'.

decisions.choice: "atajipatia" (L), "atashughulikia" (B), "atatoa" (R)
decisions.reason: "Kuona" would read as 'watch'. Literal uses the reflexive "-ji-" ("atajipatia", 'will obtain for himself'), which carries the Hebrew 'for himself' inside the verb, so no free pronoun is left for the deity pronoun setting; Balanced says "atashughulikia" ('will see to'). The same verbs return in the name of the place (verse 14).

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ אֶֽל־הַמָּקוֹם֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָֽמַר־ל֣וֹ הָאֱלֹהִים֒ וַיִּ֨בֶן שָׁ֤ם אַבְרָהָם֙ אֶת־הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וַֽיַּעֲרֹ֖ךְ אֶת־הָעֵצִ֑ים וַֽיַּעֲקֹד֙ אֶת־יִצְחָ֣ק בְּנ֔וֹ וַיָּ֤שֶׂם אֹתוֹ֙ עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ מִמַּ֖עַל לָעֵצִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And they came to the place which had said to him God, and built there Abraham the altar and arranged the wood and bound Isaac his son and put him on the altar on top of the wood.

en.L: And they came to the place of which God had told him, and Abraham built the altar there and laid the wood in order, and he bound Isaac his son and laid him on the altar on top of the wood.
en.B: They arrived at the place God had named to him. There Abraham built the altar and stacked the wood on it; then he tied up Isaac his son and placed him on the altar, above the wood.
en.R: They came to the place God had told Abraham about. Abraham built an altar there and put the wood on it. Then he tied up Isaac and placed him on the altar, on top of the wood.

es.L: Y llegaron al lugar que Dios le había dicho, y edificó allí Abraham el altar y dispuso la leña, y ató a Isaac su hijo y lo puso sobre el altar, encima de la leña.
es.B: Llegaron al lugar que Dios le había indicado. Allí Abraham construyó el altar y acomodó la leña sobre él; luego ató a su hijo Isaac y lo colocó sobre el altar, encima de la leña.
es.R: Llegaron al lugar del que Dios le había hablado a Abraham. Abraham construyó allí un altar y puso la leña encima. Luego ató a Isaac y lo puso sobre el altar, encima de la leña.

fr.L: Et ils arrivèrent au lieu dont Dieu lui avait parlé, et Abraham bâtit là l’autel et disposa le bois, et il lia Isaac son fils et le mit sur l’autel, par-dessus le bois.
fr.B: Ils arrivèrent au lieu que Dieu lui avait indiqué. Là, Abraham bâtit l’autel et y rangea le bois ; puis il attacha son fils Isaac et le plaça sur l’autel, au-dessus du bois.
fr.R: Ils sont arrivés à l’endroit dont Dieu avait parlé à Abraham. Abraham y a construit un autel et il a mis le bois dessus. Puis il a attaché Isaac et il l’a placé sur l’autel, sur le bois.

sw.L: Nao wakafika mahali ambapo Mungu alimwambia, na Abrahamu akajenga madhabahu pale, akazipanga kuni, akamfunga Isaka mwanawe, akamweka juu ya madhabahu juu ya kuni.
sw.B: Walifika mahali ambapo Mungu alikuwa amemtajia. Hapo Abrahamu akajenga madhabahu, akapanga kuni juu yake; kisha akamfunga mwanawe Isaka, akamlaza juu ya madhabahu, juu ya kuni.
sw.R: Wakafika mahali ambapo Mungu alikuwa amemwambia Abrahamu. Abrahamu akajenga madhabahu pale, akaweka kuni juu yake. Kisha akamfunga Isaka, akamweka juu ya madhabahu, juu ya kuni.

decisions.choice: bound ('aqad): tied hand and foot
decisions.reason: The verb is found only here in the Bible; it means to tie the legs of an animal for sacrifice. Jewish tradition calls this chapter the Akedah, 'the binding'. The text says nothing of any struggle, though Isaac was old enough to carry the wood (verse 6).

decisions.choice: laid the wood in order: the work of a priest
decisions.reason: The verb ('arakh) is used later of priests setting the wood and offering on the altar (Leviticus 1:7-8).

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח אַבְרָהָם֙ אֶת־יָד֔וֹ וַיִּקַּ֖ח אֶת־הַֽמַּאֲכֶ֑לֶת לִשְׁחֹ֖ט אֶת־בְּנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And stretched out Abraham his hand and took the knife to slaughter his son.

en.L: And Abraham stretched out his hand and took the knife to slaughter his son.
en.B: Abraham reached for the knife and took it in his hand, ready to slaughter his son.
en.R: Then Abraham took hold of the knife. He was ready to kill his son.

es.L: Y extendió Abraham su mano y tomó el cuchillo para degollar a su hijo.
es.B: Abraham alargó la mano y tomó el cuchillo, dispuesto a sacrificar a su hijo.
es.R: Entonces Abraham agarró el cuchillo. Estaba dispuesto a matar a su hijo.

fr.L: Et Abraham étendit la main et prit le couteau pour égorger son fils.
fr.B: Abraham tendit la main et saisit le couteau, prêt à immoler son fils.
fr.R: Alors Abraham a pris le couteau. Il était prêt à tuer son fils.

sw.L: Naye Abrahamu akanyosha mkono wake, akakitwaa kisu ili amchinje mwanawe.
sw.B: Abrahamu alinyosha mkono, akakishika kisu, tayari kumchinja mwanawe.
sw.R: Kisha Abrahamu akakishika kisu. Alikuwa tayari kumwua mwanawe.

decisions.choice: slaughter (shachat): kill as a sacrifice
decisions.reason: This is the word for slaughtering a sacrificial animal by cutting its throat (Leviticus 1:5). The story slows down to each movement of the hand.

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֵלָ֜יו מַלְאַ֤ךְ יְהוָה֙ מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אַבְרָהָ֣ם׀אַבְרָהָ֑ם וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הִנֵּֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And called to him [the] angel of YHWH from the heavens and said, Abraham, Abraham. And he said, here I [am].

en.L: But the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} called to him from heaven and said, "Abraham, Abraham!" And he said, "Here I am."
en.B: But from heaven the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} called to him, "Abraham, Abraham!" And Abraham said, "I am here."
en.R: But the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} shouted to him from heaven, "Abraham! Abraham!" Abraham answered, "Yes, I am here."

es.L: Pero el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} lo llamó desde el cielo y dijo: «¡Abraham, Abraham!». Y él dijo: «Aquí estoy».
es.B: Pero desde el cielo el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} lo llamó: «¡Abraham, Abraham!». Y Abraham respondió: «Aquí estoy».
es.R: Pero el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} le gritó desde el cielo: «¡Abraham! ¡Abraham!». Abraham contestó: «Sí, aquí estoy».

fr.L: Mais l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} l’appela du ciel et dit : « Abraham, Abraham ! » Et il dit : « Me voici. »
fr.B: Mais du ciel l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} l’appela : « Abraham, Abraham ! » Et Abraham répondit : « Je suis là. »
fr.R: Mais l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} lui a crié depuis le ciel : « Abraham ! Abraham ! » Abraham a répondu : « Oui, je suis là. »

sw.L: Lakini malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwita kutoka mbinguni, akasema, "Abrahamu, Abrahamu!" Naye akasema, "Mimi hapa."
sw.B: Lakini kutoka mbinguni malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwita, "Abrahamu, Abrahamu!" Naye Abrahamu akasema, "Niko hapa."
sw.R: Lakini malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwita kwa sauti kubwa kutoka mbinguni, "Abrahamu! Abrahamu!" Abrahamu akajibu, "Naam, niko hapa."

decisions.choice: the angel of the LORD: God speaking as his messenger
decisions.reason: As with Hagar (16:7-13; 21:17), the angel speaks as God himself: 'you have not withheld your son from me' (verse 12).

decisions.choice: Abraham, Abraham: the name twice for urgency
decisions.reason: God calls a name twice at turning points (46:2; Exodus 3:4; 1 Samuel 3:10). Here the call stops the knife.

source.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אַל־תִּשְׁלַ֤ח יָֽדְךָ֙ אֶל־הַנַּ֔עַר וְאַל־תַּ֥עַשׂ ל֖וֹ מְא֑וּמָּהכִּ֣י׀עַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֗עְתִּי כִּֽי־יְרֵ֤א אֱלֹהִים֙ אַ֔תָּה וְלֹ֥א חָשַׂ֛כְתָּ אֶת־בִּנְךָ֥ אֶת־יְחִידְךָ֖ מִמֶּֽנִּי׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, do not stretch out your hand against the lad, and do not do to him anything; for now I know that fearing God [are] you, and you have not withheld your son, your only one, from me.

en.L: And he said, "Do not stretch out your hand against the boy, or do anything to him, for now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your son, your only [son], from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.B: He said, "Keep your hand away from the boy, and do him no harm. I now know that you are one who fears God, since you have not refused {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} your son, your only son."
en.R: The angel said, "Do not hurt the boy! Do not do anything to him. Now I know that you honor God above all else. You did not keep your son, your only son, from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

es.L: Y dijo: «No extiendas tu mano contra el muchacho, ni le hagas nada, porque ahora sé que temes a Dios, ya que no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} has negado a tu hijo, a tu único».
es.B: Le dijo: «Aparta la mano del muchacho y no le hagas ningún daño. Ahora sé que eres alguien que teme a Dios, pues no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} has negado a tu hijo, tu único hijo».
es.R: El ángel le dijo: «¡No le hagas daño al muchacho! No le hagas nada. Ahora sé que honras a Dios por encima de todo. No {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} negaste a tu hijo, tu único hijo».

fr.L: Et il dit : « N’étends pas ta main contre le garçon et ne lui fais rien, car maintenant je sais que tu crains Dieu, puisque tu ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as pas refusé ton fils, ton unique. »
fr.B: Il dit : « Ne porte pas la main sur le garçon, ne lui fais aucun mal. Je sais maintenant que tu es quelqu’un qui craint Dieu, puisque tu ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as pas refusé ton fils, ton fils unique. »
fr.R: L’ange a dit : « Ne fais pas de mal au garçon ! Ne lui fais rien. Maintenant, je sais que tu honores Dieu plus que tout. Tu ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as pas refusé ton fils, ton fils unique. »

sw.L: Akasema, "Usinyoshe mkono wako juu ya kijana, wala usimtendee neno lolote, kwa maana sasa najua ya kuwa wewe unamcha Mungu, kwa kuwa hukunizuilia {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} mwanao, mwana wako wa pekee."
sw.B: Akasema, "Usimguse kijana, wala usimdhuru. Sasa najua kwamba wewe ni mtu anayemcha Mungu, kwa kuwa hukuninyima {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} mwanao, mwana wako wa pekee."
sw.R: Malaika akasema, "Usimdhuru kijana! Usimfanye chochote. Sasa najua kwamba unamheshimu Mungu kuliko kitu kingine chochote. Hukuninyima mwanao, mwana wako wa pekee."

decisions.choice: now I know: the test brings faith into the open
decisions.reason: God knows the heart, yet the test makes Abraham's faith visible in action, as a fact (Deuteronomy 8:2; James 2:21-23).

decisions.choice: you fear God: reverent trust that obeys
decisions.reason: The fear of God is reverence that puts God first. Abraham had thought there was no fear of God in Gerar (20:11); here it is proved in Abraham.

decisions.choice: from me: the angel speaks as God
decisions.reason: The angel says that Isaac was not withheld 'from me': the offering was made to God, and God speaks through his messenger.

decisions.choice: you honor God above all else
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of 'fear God' here, which is not terror but a reverence that holds nothing back (m2).

source.text: וַיִּשָּׂ֨א אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֶת־עֵינָ֗יו וַיַּרְא֙ וְהִנֵּה־אַ֔יִל אַחַ֕ר נֶאֱחַ֥ז בַּסְּבַ֖ךְ בְּקַרְנָ֑יו וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ אַבְרָהָם֙ וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֶת־הָאַ֔יִל וַיַּעֲלֵ֥הוּ לְעֹלָ֖ה תַּ֥חַת בְּנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And lifted Abraham his eyes and saw, and behold, a ram behind [him] caught in the thicket by its horns; and went Abraham and took the ram and offered it up as a burnt offering in place of his son.

en.L: And Abraham lifted up his eyes and looked, and there behind [him] was a ram caught in a thicket by its horns. And Abraham went and took the ram and offered it up as a burnt offering in place of his son.
en.B: When Abraham raised his eyes, he saw a ram behind him, held fast in the brush by its horns. So he went and took the ram, and offered it up as a burnt offering in his son's place.
en.R: Abraham looked around and saw a ram behind him. Its horns were caught in some bushes. So Abraham went and got the ram. He sacrificed the ram on the altar instead of Isaac, as a burnt offering.

es.L: Y alzó Abraham sus ojos y miró, y he aquí detrás [de él] un carnero trabado en un matorral por sus cuernos. Y fue Abraham y tomó el carnero y lo ofreció en holocausto en lugar de su hijo.
es.B: Cuando Abraham levantó la vista, vio detrás de él un carnero enredado por los cuernos en la maleza. Fue, tomó el carnero y lo ofreció en holocausto en lugar de su hijo.
es.R: Abraham miró a su alrededor y vio detrás de él un carnero. Tenía los cuernos enredados en unos arbustos. Abraham fue y agarró el carnero. Lo sacrificó sobre el altar en lugar de Isaac, como holocausto.

fr.L: Et Abraham leva les yeux et regarda, et voici, derrière [lui], un bélier pris par ses cornes dans un fourré. Et Abraham alla prendre le bélier et l’offrit en holocauste à la place de son fils.
fr.B: Quand Abraham leva les yeux, il vit derrière lui un bélier retenu par les cornes dans les broussailles. Il alla prendre le bélier et l’offrit en holocauste à la place de son fils.
fr.R: Abraham a regardé autour de lui et il a vu un bélier derrière lui. Ses cornes étaient prises dans des buissons. Abraham est allé prendre le bélier. Il l’a sacrifié sur l’autel à la place d’Isaac, en holocauste.

sw.L: Naye Abrahamu akainua macho yake, akatazama, na tazama, nyuma [yake] kondoo dume amenaswa kichakani kwa pembe zake. Abrahamu akaenda, akamtwaa yule kondoo dume, akamtoa kuwa sadaka ya kuteketezwa mahali pa mwanawe.
sw.B: Abrahamu alipoinua macho, alimwona nyuma yake kondoo dume aliyenaswa pembe zake vichakani. Akaenda, akamchukua yule kondoo dume, akamtoa kuwa sadaka ya kuteketezwa badala ya mwanawe.
sw.R: Abrahamu alitazama pande zote, akaona kondoo dume nyuma yake. Pembe zake zilikuwa zimekwama katika vichaka. Abrahamu akaenda, akamchukua yule kondoo dume. Akamtoa sadaka juu ya madhabahu badala ya Isaka, kuwa sadaka ya kuteketezwa.

decisions.choice: behind (achar): or 'one' (echad)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word 'behind' differs from 'one' only by the shape of one letter. The Samaritan Pentateuch, many Hebrew manuscripts, the Septuagint and the Syriac read 'a ram' or 'one ram'. The standard Hebrew text, followed here, has 'behind'.

decisions.choice: in place of his son: a substitute
decisions.reason: The ram dies instead of Isaac. The idea of one life given in place of another runs through Israel's sacrifices and is taken up in the New Testament (Romans 8:32, which echoes verse 12).

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֧א אַבְרָהָ֛ם שֵֽׁם־הַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא יְהוָ֣ה׀יִרְאֶ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֙ יֵאָמֵ֣ר הַיּ֔וֹם בְּהַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה יֵרָאֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And called Abraham [the] name of that place YHWH-will-see, as it is said today, on [the] mountain of YHWH it will be seen.

en.L: And Abraham called the name of that place "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} Will Provide," as it is said to this day, "On the mountain of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} it will be provided."
en.B: Abraham named that place "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} Will See to It." That is why people still say today, "On the mountain of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} it will be seen to."
en.R: Abraham named that place "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} Will Provide." Even today people say, "On the mountain of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, what is needed will be provided."

es.L: Y llamó Abraham el nombre de aquel lugar «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} proveerá», como se dice hasta hoy: «En el monte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} será provisto».
es.B: Abraham llamó a aquel lugar «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se encargará». Por eso todavía hoy se dice: «En el monte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, él se encargará».
es.R: Abraham le puso a aquel lugar el nombre «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} proveerá». Todavía hoy la gente dice: «En el monte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} se dará lo que haga falta».

fr.L: Et Abraham appela ce lieu du nom de « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} pourvoira », comme on dit encore aujourd’hui : « Sur la montagne {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, il sera pourvu. »

decisions.choice: The LORD Will Provide: literally 'the LORD will see'
decisions.reason: The name takes up Abraham's words to Isaac, 'God will see for himself the lamb' (verse 8): the LORD saw to it, and provided. Hagar had named God 'the God who sees' (16:13).

decisions.choice: it will be provided: or 'he will be seen'
decisions.reason: The last verb is the passive of 'see'. It can mean 'it will be seen to' (provided), or 'he will be seen', that is, the LORD appears on his mountain. The saying plays on both senses.

decisions.choice: the mountain of the LORD
decisions.reason: Later the phrase names the temple mount in Jerusalem (Isaiah 2:3; Psalm 24:3), which 2 Chronicles 3:1 calls Mount Moriah.

decisions.choice: Will Provide (L, R), Will See to It (B)
decisions.reason: The name is translated so the reader can see its link with verse 8; Balanced keeps the verb 'see'. The older form 'Jehovah-jireh' only transliterates the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: "proveerá" (L, R), "se encargará" (B); the saying "será provisto" (L), "él se encargará" (B)
decisions.reason: The name repeats Abraham's words to Isaac in verse 8, so it uses the same Spanish verbs. "Encargarse" has no natural passive, so Balanced says "él se encargará" for 'it will be seen to'.

decisions.choice: "pourvoira" (L, R), "y veillera" (B); the saying "il sera pourvu" (L), "on y veillera" (B)
decisions.reason: The name repeats Abraham's words to Isaac in verse 8, so it uses the same French verbs. French has no passive of "veiller à", so Balanced turns 'it will be seen to' into the impersonal "on y veillera".

decisions.choice: "Atatoa" (L, R), "Atashughulikia" (B); the saying "itatolewa" (L), "itashughulikiwa" (B)
decisions.reason: The name repeats Abraham's words to Isaac in verse 8 ("atajipatia", "atashughulikia", "atatoa"), and Swahili's passive forms keep the saying's impersonal 'it will be provided' at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: by myself I have sworn: God's strongest promise
decisions.reason: This is the only time in the stories of the patriarchs that God swears an oath. Having no one greater to swear by, he swears by himself (Hebrews 6:13-18). Later generations recall 'the oath to Abraham' (26:3; 50:24).

decisions.choice: declares the LORD (ne'um YHWH)
decisions.reason: This phrase, very common in the prophets, appears here for the first time. It marks the words as a solemn statement from God himself.

fr.L: que je te bénirai assurément, et que je multiplierai assurément ta descendance comme les étoiles des cieux et comme le sable qui est sur la rive de la mer. Et ta descendance prendra possession de la porte de ses ennemis,

sw.L: hakika nitakubariki, na hakika nitauongeza sana uzao wako kama nyota za angani na kama mchanga ulio ufuoni mwa bahari. Na uzao wako utaliteka lango la adui zake,

decisions.choice: I will surely bless ... surely multiply: doubled verbs
decisions.reason: Each verb is doubled ('blessing I will bless, multiplying I will multiply') for emphasis and certainty.

decisions.choice: like the stars ... like the sand: the earlier promises
decisions.reason: God had compared Abraham's offspring to the dust of the earth (13:16) and the stars (15:5). Jacob recalls this promise of 'the sand of the sea' (32:13).

decisions.choice: possess the gate of his enemies: capture their cities
decisions.reason: The gate was a city's defense and seat of power; to hold it was to hold the city. 'His' enemies is singular, since 'offspring' is a single noun for many; Galatians 3:16 draws on the singular of 'offspring' to point to one descendant, Christ.

decisions.choice: descendants ... their enemies
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use 'descendants', as elsewhere, and so 'their'; Literal keeps 'offspring' and the singular 'his' (m3).

decisions.choice: shall be blessed in your offspring: blessing reaches the nations through Abraham's line
alternatives: shall bless themselves by your offspring (shall pray to be blessed as they are)
decisions.reason: The verb form here (hitbarakhu) is usually reflexive, 'bless themselves': the nations would say 'may God bless us as he blessed them'. This translation reads it with the passive of 12:3 and 18:18, as the Septuagint does and as the New Testament quotes the promise (Acts 3:25). On either reading the nations' blessing is bound up with Abraham's offspring.

decisions.choice: because you have listened to my voice: obedience
decisions.reason: The promise was given freely in 12:1-3; now God confirms it with an oath because Abraham obeyed. God repeats it to Isaac for the same reason (26:5).

decisions.choice: Abraham returned: Isaac is not mentioned
decisions.reason: The narrator names only Abraham. Isaac surely came down with him ('we will come back', verse 5), but the story ends with the father alone in view, and Isaac is not mentioned again until his marriage is arranged (24:4).

decisions.choice: Milcah too: like Sarah
decisions.reason: Milcah was the wife of Abraham's brother Nahor (11:29). 'She too' sets her beside Sarah, who has just had a son. The news prepares for the search for a wife for Isaac.

decisions.choice: Uz, Buz: names of peoples to the east
decisions.reason: Uz is the land of Job (Job 1:1), and Elihu, one of his friends, was a Buzite (Job 32:2); Jeremiah names Uz and Buz among the peoples east of Israel (Jeremiah 25:20, 23).

decisions.reason: 'Father' here means ancestor or founder. Nahor's family lived in Aram, in the north (24:10; 25:20). Another Aram appears among the sons of Shem (10:22-23).

records.literal_gloss: And Bethuel fathered Rebekah. These eight bore Milcah to Nahor, [the] brother of Abraham.

en.L: And Bethuel fathered Rebekah. These eight Milcah bore to Nahor, Abraham's brother.
en.B: Bethuel was the father of Rebekah. These eight were the sons Milcah bore to Nahor, Abraham's brother.
en.R: Bethuel was the father of Rebekah. Milcah had these eight sons with Nahor, Abraham's brother.

es.L: Y Betuel engendró a Rebeca. Estos ocho dio a luz Milca a Nacor, hermano de Abraham.
es.B: Betuel fue el padre de Rebeca. Estos fueron los ocho hijos que Milca le dio a Nacor, el hermano de Abraham.
es.R: Betuel era el padre de Rebeca. Milca tuvo estos ocho hijos con Nacor, el hermano de Abraham.

fr.L: Et Bethouël engendra Rébecca. Ces huit-là, Milka les enfanta à Nahor, frère d’Abraham.
fr.B: Bethouël fut le père de Rébecca. Tels furent les huit fils que Milka donna à Nahor, le frère d’Abraham.
fr.R: Bethouël était le père de Rébecca. Milka a eu ces huit fils avec Nahor, le frère d’Abraham.

sw.L: Naye Bethueli akamzaa Rebeka. Hawa wanane Milka alimzalia Nahori, ndugu wa Abrahamu.
sw.B: Bethueli alikuwa baba wa Rebeka. Hao ndio wana wanane ambao Milka alimzalia Nahori, ndugu wa Abrahamu.
sw.R: Bethueli alikuwa baba wa Rebeka. Milka alimzalia Nahori, ndugu wa Abrahamu, wana hao wanane.

decisions.choice: Rebekah: the next mother of the promise
decisions.reason: Of all the names in the list only one granddaughter is named: Rebekah, who will become Isaac's wife (chapter 24). Right after the promise of offspring (verse 17), the narrator shows where it will continue.

source.text: וּפִֽילַגְשׁ֖וֹ וּשְׁמָ֣הּ רְאוּמָ֑ה וַתֵּ֤לֶד גַּם־הִוא֙ אֶת־טֶ֣בַח וְאֶת־גַּ֔חַם וְאֶת־תַּ֖חַשׁ וְאֶֽת־מַעֲכָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And his concubine, and her name [was] Reumah, and bore also she Tebah and Gaham and Tahash and Maacah.

en.L: And his concubine, whose name was Reumah, also bore Tebah, and Gaham, and Tahash, and Maacah.
en.B: Nahor also had a secondary wife named Reumah, and she bore him Tebah, Gaham, Tahash and Maacah.
en.R: Nahor also had another wife, of lower rank, named Reumah. She had four sons: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash and Maacah.

es.L: Y su concubina, cuyo nombre [era] Reúma, también dio a luz a Tebá, y a Gaham, y a Tahas, y a Maacá.
es.B: Nacor tuvo además una esposa secundaria llamada Reúma, que le dio a Tebá, Gaham, Tahas y Maacá.
es.R: Nacor tenía también otra esposa, de menor rango, llamada Reúma. Ella tuvo cuatro hijos: Tebá, Gaham, Tahas y Maacá.

fr.L: Et sa concubine, dont le nom [était] Réouma, enfanta elle aussi Téba, et Gaham, et Tahash, et Maaka.
fr.B: Nahor avait aussi une épouse de second rang, nommée Réouma, qui lui donna Téba, Gaham, Tahash et Maaka.
fr.R: Nahor avait aussi une autre femme, d’un rang moins élevé, qui s’appelait Réouma. Elle a eu quatre fils : Téba, Gaham, Tahash et Maaka.

sw.L: Na suria wake, ambaye jina lake [lilikuwa] Reuma, naye akazaa Teba, na Gahamu, na Tahashi, na Maaka.
sw.B: Nahori alikuwa pia na mke mdogo aitwaye Reuma, naye akamzalia Teba, Gahamu, Tahashi na Maaka.
sw.R: Nahori pia alikuwa na mke mwingine, wa cheo cha chini, jina lake Reuma. Yeye alizaa wana wanne: Teba, Gahamu, Tahashi na Maaka.

decisions.choice: concubine (pilegesh): a wife of lower rank
decisions.reason: A concubine was a lawful partner of lower status than a full wife; her sons could be given gifts but not an equal share of the inheritance (25:6).

decisions.choice: twelve sons in all
decisions.reason: Eight sons by Milcah and four by Reumah make twelve, like the twelve sons of Ishmael (25:13-16) and of Jacob (35:22-26).

decisions.choice: secondary wife (B), another wife, of lower rank (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the word means; 'concubine' can suggest a mistress, which is not what is meant (m1).
